records.text: B'nai B'rith became the Anti-Defamation League after the murder of Mary Phagan.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That then subsequently became the ADL after the ritualistic murder of a Catholic girl named Mary Phagan. There was no hiding that anymore.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The ADL's own 1913 founding charter and historical accounts show it was founded under B'nai B'rith before Leo Frank's August 1915 lynching. The Frank case influenced the organization's early context and growth, but the ADL did not come into existence after the murder.

sources.title: Anti-Defamation League Founding Charter (1913)
sources.relevance: Primary organizational document directly dates the ADL's founding to 1913, contradicting the claim that it arose after the 1915 murder.

records.text: Candace Owens said the ADL annually argues that antisemitism caused Leo Frank's conviction and has sought for decades to overturn it
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Yet to this day, every year the ADL lobbies, claims it was anti-Semitism that he got convicted, or there was none, he was an unbelievably powerful player, and he was also convicted by a jury that consisted of Jews. ... And they have been attempting to get that conviction overturned for decades.

verification.notes: ADL materials do argue that antisemitism influenced Frank's conviction and describe efforts that produced a posthumous pardon; the pardon did not exonerate him. The broader claims that ADL makes this argument annually and has sought every year for decades to overturn the conviction were not substantiated by the available sources.

records.text: Charlie Kirk said that if Anti-Defamation League people told him to get rid of Candace Owens, he told them to lose his number if they had anything to say about her.
records.speaker: Charlie Kirk

appearances.snippet: He was not just saying this privately. People have shared clips of him saying the same publicly. He said, "If ADL people are telling me to get rid of Candace (Candace Owens), I told them to lose my number if they have anything to say about Candace (Candace Owens)."

verification.notes: Transcript context at 00:06:05 was reviewed. A later transcript reproduces the underlying November 2023 audio in which Kirk says he told a critic of Owens's continued AmFest participation to lose his number. That supports the substance of the quoted defense of Owens, but the underlying audio describes the critic only as a lunatic and does not identify the person as an ADL representative. The ADL-specific portion is therefore unconfirmed.
